parts.t: RECIPE 03 — Claude Cowork: you already know most of it
From: Claude Cowork 60 Minute MASTERCLASS 🤯 · 9 Apr 2026 · 1:01:12 · watch
**You asked: "see if I already know it." I read all 11,830 words.**
Rewritten 12 Sep after the original was lost to a git operation by another session. Same source, same content.
The answer: yes, mostly. Do not spend the hour.
Roughly 70% of it is things you do without thinking.
The one idea worth the hour — and it is YOUR problem

"if there is a task that you are repeating again and again, that should be turned into a skill. Or if you have a task with a set of preferences, guidelines, and rules, that should also be turned into a skill.
" "Because you don't want to explain your preferences every time."
You are already half-doing it — nine of your own: ebay-listing, notion-summary, digital-product, board, pickup, recap, rule, summarise, videos.
So the takeaway is not "learn skills". It is: the next time you catch yourself repeating an instruction to me, that is a skill waiting to be written.
The four things you are probably NOT using
1 · Dispatch — run it from your phone, reaching your computer
"you could be waiting at a doctor's office or waiting in line somewhere and tell Cowork, 'grab the last three photos I took or grab something from my downloads folder and post it to LinkedIn.'"
This is the one both reviewers split on today. GPT flagged that its relationship to your protected Remote Control setup is unresolved. Do not set it up blind.
2 · Skills are composable
"you can have one skill that knows it should use a bunch of other skills."
Both reviewers said DROP this for now — chaining removes the moment where you check the first skill's output before the second eats it.
3 · Ideas — Anthropic's own suggestion list
"if you really have no idea where to start, I recommend just going to ideas."
Both reviewers said drop this too: a panel that suggests more things to do is the last thing for someone with a backlog.
4 · "Allow" vs "Always allow"
"If you're a beginner to this, I recommend clicking allow, not always allow... AI has access to your computer, which is powerful but potentially dangerous."
She then clicks "always allow" herself for filming and says not to copy her. You audited this today: 31 auto-approved, zero blocked.
What to ignore
All five of her use cases run on Blotato — her own $29/month product. The social-calendar section is a demo, and you do not post to social media as a business.

One technical detail worth keeping: local files went straight from her computer to the publishing tool. "You don't have to use an intermediate storage solution like Google Drive, Dropbox, or Amazon S3.
" That four-step dance is a real annoyance in many tools.
What to try — ten minutes, free
ALSO MENTIONED
Her plan: "I'm on the Max plan... most often just in Opus 4.6". For $20/month users
she recommends Sonnet or Haiku and extended thinking off
Her path: *"start with Cowork... once you master Cowork, it's not a huge leap to
transition to Claude Code"*
The clearest line in the video: *"with ChatGPT... you the human have to still do it. The
difference with Cowork is... it does all of the things for you"*
See also
RECIPE 01 — the same Blotato build in Claude Code. Read one, not both.
